title: Data centre plan in Cardiff could be powered by gas power plant
key_facts: The developer, Curtis Hall, says it is also seeking permission to build a temporary gas power plant for a proposed data centre at the Cardiff East Park and Ride site near Llanrumney, which it says is a 'worst-case scenario' (BBC).

Planning documents describe a 'temporary ancillary energy centre' with a maximum capacity of 49.9 megawatts, starting in July 2028 and running about five years, until July 2033, with five gas turbines, a steam generator and two standby turbines.
In the long term the data centre needs a 150-megawatt grid connection, which may not be delivered until between 2030 and 2034; about 40 diesel backup generators would also be needed after connection.
Energy plants of 50 megawatts or more need Welsh government planning permission; Curtis Hall denied limiting the plant to 49.9 megawatts to avoid that.
Friends of the Earth Cymru calls it 'climate-wrecking'; almost all the area's Members of the Senedd, a Welsh government minister and a senior Labour councillor have objected.

The Welsh government is considering taking over the planning process, which stops Cardiff Council deciding in the meantime, and plans to publish its own data-centre policy by the end of the year; a council consultation runs until 28 October.

The company says the technology is 'not confirmed' and could be fuel cells, and that the gas plant would not be needed if the grid connection arrives in time; nearby residents worry about noise, fumes and the University Hospital of Wales.
quote_evidence: The developer of a proposed data centre in Cardiff has said it is also seeking permission to build a gas power plant to get it up and running.
Developer Curtis Hall said the plant, which could operate for up to five years, may be needed if the site cannot get on the national grid quick enough.
The Welsh government is considering whether it will take over the planning process for the facility - meaning Cardiff Council is unable to grant planning permission in the meantime.
why_it_matters_hint: A data centre that cannot get grid power quickly may build its own gas plant, which is drawing objections from local politicians and residents and a possible Welsh government takeover of the decision.
notes: The article does not date when the developer first disclosed the gas plan. Single outlet, but based on planning documents and named statements.
